page: Microsoft Azure NV24ads_V710_v5 is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The instance combines dedicated x86_64 host resources with dedicated graphics acceleration, featuring 24 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD processor alongside 128 GB of system memory, providing approximately 5.33 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is provided by a single AMD V710 GPU equipped with 24 GB of dedicated video memory.

Storage configuration includes an integrated 1649 GB local NVMe solid-state drive, enabling low-latency temporary caching and scratchpad operations directly adjacent to the compute cores. The instance also supports Azure Premium Storage for external disk requirements. Network connectivity provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating standard virtual network configuration or private routing for internet-facing access.

From an architectural standpoint, the combination of a 24 GB AMD V710 GPU with a high-capacity local NVMe disk provides balanced computational throughput and fast local I/O without requiring dedicated external storage arrays for high-throughput temporary assets. While it lacks specialized enterprise deep learning hardware like large scale accelerator clusters, its resource profile delivers solid density for graphics-intensive and visualization tasks. The server type is well configured for virtual desktop infrastructure, remote workstations, 3D visualization, interactive rendering, and video processing pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure NV24ads_V710_v5 is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine designed for graphics-intensive compute and visualization workloads. It features 24 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs powered by an AMD processor, 128 GB of system memory delivering 5.33 GB per vCPU, and a dedicated AMD V710 GPU equipped with 24 GB of VRAM. For local high-speed I/O, the instance includes an integrated 1649 GB local NVMe SSD, complemented by support for Azure Premium Storage disks. Networking configurations omit complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The balance of 24 dedicated compute cores, generous system RAM, fast local solid-state storage, and dedicated AMD graphics hardware makes this instance an effective platform for remote workstation deployments, virtual desktop infrastructure, interactive 3D rendering, video encoding, and GPU-assisted engineering simulations.
